1.stem: [Academic Talk — Architectural History] According to the professor, what did the laser scan show about the shape of the priory's tower?

options.A: The tower leans by a small but consistent amount toward the southwest
options.B: The tower's cross-section is slightly oval rather than round, wider along the river face
options.C: Its upper stage sits slightly off the axis of the stages beneath it
options.D: Its courses undulate in a way consistent with ground movement while building was under way

2.stem: [Academic Talk — Lexicography] Why does the professor dwell on the entry for a dialect name for a fishing float?

options.A: Its evidence came from a single county, which forced a decision about regional labels
options.B: It was reset in type after the first proof, needing a second pass unlike its neighboring entries
options.C: Its definition survives in six successive drafts, which show the house style taking shape
options.D: An error in its etymology outlived four printings, showing how slowly corrections spread

3.stem: [Academic Talk — Naval History] According to the professor, what did the survey of trial-day coal returns across the fleet show?

options.A: Ships tried in the winter months returned higher figures than those tried in summer
options.B: Burning on the day sat well below what the same vessels used in ordinary service
options.C: The returns were made up in measures that differed from yard to yard and went unreconciled
options.D: Consumption varied more between stokehold crews than between the ships they served in

4.stem: [Academic Talk — Architectural History] Why does the professor discuss the mason's marks in the priory's choir?

options.A: Their placement lets the team assign stretches of walling to particular building seasons
options.B: Their spacing offers a check on the unit of length the medieval masons worked to
options.C: One of them recurs at a quarry the team recorded, tying the choir's stone to a source
options.D: They cluster where the fabric shows rebuilding, which helps put a date to the repairs

5.stem: [Academic Talk — Mycology] What is the professor's position on the claim that the fungus is spreading northward?

options.A: She suspects the old southern finds were misnamed, and that the range was northern from the start
options.B: She grants a real expansion, but one tracking the river valleys rather than heading north as such
options.C: She reads the apparent spread as a product of wider sampling, not of any shift in range
options.D: She credits it, chiefly because sites added in the north have begun to turn it up

6.stem: [Academic Talk — Mycology] Why does the professor mention the orchard at Hedravean?

options.A: Its mapped and managed trees gave the team a known population to calibrate against
options.B: It carries the fungus through repeated sprayings, a pressure the forest stands are spared
options.C: A long run of harvest records from it lets past outbreaks be given dates
options.D: Complaints from its growers were what first drew the team's attention to the fungus

7.stem: [Academic Talk — Mycology] According to the professor, what did the samplers show about how far the spores carry from an infected stand?

options.A: The catch falls away within a few hundred metres of an infected stand
options.B: The catch runs heaviest at middling distances, and thinner both close in and far out
options.C: The catch holds up across several kilometres of ground, thinning slowly with distance
options.D: The catch showed no steady relation to distance, tracking the height of the collector instead

8.stem: [Academic Talk — Herpetology] What did the professor say the recapture figures showed about the population estimate?

options.A: Estimates from the spring sessions ran well above the autumn ones for the same reach
options.B: The estimate climbed year on year until the season the trapping effort was cut back
options.C: Figures from the two ends of the valley moved independently of each other
options.D: Animals reappeared far sooner after release than the model said they should

9.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Photography] According to the professor, what did records of a rival studio in the same town show about its pricing of portrait sittings?

options.A: It charged a flat fee regardless of how many prints were ordered, unlike Morgelly's per-print scale
options.B: It kept single sittings level with Morgelly's rates but undercut him for group portraits
options.C: Its prices climbed each time a new photographic process reached the town, tracking material costs
options.D: It advertised fixed rates yet routinely discounted them for return customers, a practice its own books record

10.stem: [Academic Talk — Lexicography] According to the professor, what did the recount of the citation slips in the boxes show?

options.A: The collection grew fastest in the years the annual reports describe as lean
options.B: The published counts overstate the holdings for the letters late in the alphabet
options.C: Boxes for the commonest words had been thinned at some point, with the discards going unrecorded
options.D: Material in the earliest hands sat misfiled under spellings a reform had since changed

11.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Medicine] Why does the professor bring up the ledger kept by the Trelundy infirmary's dispenser?

options.A: Marginal notes in it preserve queries the dispenser raised about dosages the prescribing physicians had set
options.B: A gap in its pages is the chief evidence for when the scheme was interrupted
options.C: It shows the practice cost enough that the governors debated giving it up more than once
options.D: Its running totals let historians work out how many beds the house actually kept filled

12.stem: [Academic Talk — Lexicography] What does the professor suggest scholars will be able to do once the project's archive is catalogued?

options.A: Establish how the work was shared out, from the marks each editor left on the material
options.B: Compare the finished definitions with the rival wordbook the chief editor kept annotating
options.C: Date when particular senses first drew notice, from the postmarks the incoming packets carry
options.D: Recover entries written and then cut before the parts went to the printer

13.stem: [Academic Talk — Herpetology] What does the professor imply about the team's plans for identifying individual salamanders?

options.A: They will keep the tags and the photographs in use together for several more seasons
options.B: They will go on tagging adults but release the juveniles without processing
options.C: They will move to a tag that can be read at a distance, without handling
options.D: They will give up the physical tags and rely on each animal's spot pattern

14.stem: [Academic Talk — Architectural History] What does the professor imply the recording team intends to do next?

options.A: Put the scan through a structural model, to test what the tower can still safely carry
options.B: Repeat the scan after an interval long enough to test how repeatable its readings are
options.C: Move on to the parish's other early buildings to give the priory a comparison
options.D: Extend the scanning into the roof spaces, which the first campaign left untouched

15.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Photography] Why does the professor set the ledger beside the price lists of the plate makers?

options.A: To show the exposure figures shortening just as faster plates came onto the market
options.B: To trace his suppliers, since the studio's own purchase papers do not survive
options.C: To show he kept ordering a line the catalogues had dropped some years before
options.D: To argue that selling supplies on the side earned him more than the camera work did

16.stem: [Academic Talk — Naval History] Where does the professor stand on Nansveor's charge that trial speeds were inflated across the fleet?

options.A: He turns it around: reported speeds ran low, so owners kept a margin to reveal later
options.B: He endorses the charge, and adds that the habit sharpened as newspaper interest grew
options.C: He rejects a deliberate design, tracing the excess to a current allowance applied the wrong way
options.D: He allows it for the export orders, while home trials he takes as recorded straight

17.stem: [Academic Talk — Sedimentology] According to the professor, what did Ordwell's replotting of the old soundings reveal?

options.A: The filling-in after each dredging ran quickest the first winter and slackened after that
options.B: Stations the books list under a single name turn out to have moved between crews
options.C: Patches of shoal came and went within a year, faster than the annual visits could catch
options.D: The deepest water had shifted toward the town shore, and by more than had been supposed

18.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Medicine] What is the professor's view of Rostrellick's claim that the weighing shaped who was admitted?

options.A: He rejects it, since admission rested with subscribers kept at arm's length from the data
options.B: He holds the surviving papers cannot settle it until the admission registers are worked through
options.C: He grants a narrower version, with the weighing shaping who was kept on rather than taken in
options.D: He accepts it, pointing to admission notes that discuss a candidate's likely response to the regimen

19.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Photography] What is the professor's response to Chelvern's argument that the ledger was written up after the fact for advertisement?

options.A: She accepts it, reading the uniform hand across the pages as a sign the book was copied out afterward for display
options.B: She rejects it, pointing to shifts of ink from entry to entry that fit a book kept daily
options.C: She accepts it for the earliest volume, which she reads as reconstructed at a stroke from memory
options.D: She leaves it open, since the surviving pages give no way to tell entry date from copying date

20.stem: [Academic Talk — Sedimentology] What is the professor's central claim about what the silt record of the Marnstow estuary shows?

options.A: The channel swings on a rhythm too slow for one engineer's term of office to take in
options.B: The estuary has run steadier than its reputation, which rests on a few remembered groundings
options.C: Much of the apparent change reflects the board measuring where its case was best served
options.D: The shoaling follows the works along the banks more closely than anything the river brings down

21.stem: [Academic Talk — Lexicography] What is the professor's position on Lensham's claim that the prefaces to each part were written to answer the reviewers?

options.A: She allows it from the middle parts onward, the earlier prefaces being pitched at the volunteer helpers
options.B: She agrees, matching several passages in them to notices that had appeared in the quarterlies
options.C: She disputes it, taking the prefaces to address the subscribers whose payments the parts depended on
options.D: She takes their audience to have been the editorial staff, with reviewers answered by letter

22.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Medicine] According to the professor, what did Maderwyn's re-examination of the weight registers find?

options.A: Patients taken in over the winter gained at rates the summer intake did not approach
options.B: Books kept by different attendants ran too nearly alike to be independent records
options.C: Weight and length of stay tracked one another less closely than contemporary reports claimed
options.D: The recorded gains cluster at round figures, a sign readings were rounded before entry

23.stem: [Academic Talk — Architectural History] What is the professor's main point about the survey of Lanmorick priory made in the 1840s?

options.A: Its measurements follow the restorers' brief, recording what the planned works needed and little more
options.B: Its lasting value lies in what it caught by accident, parts of the fabric lost soon afterward
options.C: It deserves more trust than the drawings made from it, which tidied irregularities the field books preserve
options.D: It served as a training exercise, and its errors follow the order in which the pupils worked

24.stem: [Academic Talk — Herpetology] What is the professor's central claim about what the long-running survey has measured?

options.A: A genuine decline, though one confined to the biggest size classes rather than the whole
options.B: A slow shuttling between the gorge floor and the slopes, read by earlier workers as loss
options.C: Mostly the habits of the observers, whose favored stretches supply the bulk of the detections
options.D: Less the population than a readiness to enter traps, which swings with the weather

25.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Medicine] What is the professor's central point about the infirmary's weekly weighing of patients?

options.A: The balance itself was replaced twice, and the published tables splice readings that are not comparable
options.B: Physicians read the charts as tracking recovery, while the ward staff had other ends in view
options.C: It began as a check on the kitchen's provisioning and drifted into a diagnostic habit
options.D: Its findings mattered less than its rhythm, which reorganized the week around a fixed appointment

26.stem: [Academic Talk — Naval History] What does the professor suggest the newly catalogued papers from the builders' yard are likely to show?

options.A: How far the marker posts had strayed from the distance the charts assigned them
options.B: How thoroughly the firm rehearsed the runs beforehand with a sister ship
options.C: Whether the Penvorran ran with her intended propellers or a set borrowed for the day
options.D: What the builders privately took the ship's draught to be on the morning in question

27.stem: [Academic Talk — History of Photography] What is the professor's central point about what the ledger offers historians?

options.A: It registers the sitters as much as the light, since the settings shift with who sat
options.B: It preserves one man's judgment of light, usable as an instrument once his habits are known
options.C: Its chief use is for dating his surviving prints, which entries can pin to within a week
options.D: It shows a provincial practice adopting the handbook numbers years ahead of the trade press

28.stem: [Academic Talk — Naval History] Why does the professor describe the arrangements at the measured mile off Aberwynt?

options.A: To identify the shore observers whose sightings produced the timings the navy released
options.B: To explain why its results and those from the rival ground at Porthlenny resist comparison
options.C: To trace how a new civilian pier forced the course to be shifted and surveyed afresh
options.D: To bring out how much of its upkeep fell on the port authority instead of the navy

29.stem: [Academic Talk — Mycology] What does the professor imply the team will change in next season's survey?

options.A: Keep collecting through the winter months instead of stopping in the autumn
options.B: Shift part of the effort from the interior of each plot toward its edges
options.C: Replace the sticky slides with a filter cartridge that a machine can read
options.D: Set a rain gauge beside each collector so catches can be read against the weather

30.stem: [Academic Talk — Herpetology] How does the professor respond to Polgrenna's suggestion that the salamanders breed at a second, undiscovered site?

options.A: He doubts it, taking the young to be carried down from the known pools in high water
options.B: He thinks it may hold in wet years, while in dry ones the known pools suffice
options.C: He resists it, since the young arrive in one short pulse rather than in scattered waves
options.D: He credits it, mainly because young turn up in the counts before eggs are seen locally

31.stem: [Academic Talk — Sedimentology] Why does the professor bring up the ferry slip at Fenrith?

options.A: Its rebuilding supplies a firm date against which nearby measurements can be tried
options.B: Its keeper's private depth notes cover the years the official series leaves blank
options.C: A dated painting of it shows the water standing at a mark the series can be checked against
options.D: A dispute over its silting produced sworn testimony about how the soundings were taken

32.stem: [Academic Talk — Sedimentology] What does the professor imply the research group will do with the soundings series?

options.A: Publish the raw books themselves rather than the smoothed tables put out at the time
options.B: Carry it further back by working the older harbor charts onto the modern datum
options.C: Core the reaches the record marks as gaining fastest, to test it against the mud
options.D: Run the old lead line beside the current gear for a season to learn how they differ
